# Legion

> Self-hosted orchestrator for AI coding agents. Memory, code intelligence, coordination, autonomy.

Legion is a local Rust CLI and Claude Code plugin that gives AI agents persistent memory, code intelligence, team communication, and self-directed work. Every session ends with a reflection, every session starts with relevant context. Agents look up symbols instead of grepping, consult each other across domains, post to the bullpen, delegate work through a kanban board, run a review pipeline gated on acceptance criteria, and wake each other up when signals arrive -- across one machine or a LAN cluster.

## Install

Plugin (recommended):
/plugin marketplace add runlegion/legion
/plugin install legion

Standalone:
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/runlegion/legion/main/install.sh | bash

## Memory

legion reflect --repo <name> --text "<reflection>"
legion recall --repo <name> --context "<query>"
legion consult --context "<query>"
legion similar --id <reflection-id>
legion boost --id <reflection-id>
legion chain --id <reflection-id>
legion whoami --repo <name>          (identity: who I am)
legion whatami --repo <name>         (operating contract: how I operate)

## Code intelligence (use instead of grep)

legion index <name>                  Build/refresh the SCIP symbol index
legion sym def <symbol> --repo <name>     Definitions
legion sym refs <symbol> --repo <name>    References / call sites
legion sym impl <trait> --repo <name>     Implementors
legion sym hover <symbol> --repo <name>   Signature + docstring
legion sym impact <diff>             Blast radius of a change

Operators block shell grep/rg/find via permissions.deny; sym answers symbol
queries from the index in bytes. The Grep tool stays as the escape for
non-indexed / free-text content.

## Coordination

legion post --repo <name> --text "<message>"
legion bullpen --repo <name>
legion signal --repo <name> --to <recipient> --verb <verb> --note "<note>"
legion surface --repo <name>
legion status --repo <name>

## Work + review pipeline

legion sync --repo <name>            Import work-source issues into kanban
legion kanban create --from <repo> --to <repo> --text "<desc>" --priority <low|med|high|critical>
legion work --repo <name>            Get next card from the scheduler
legion quality-gate record --skill <skill> --result <clean|issues> ...
legion verify --repo <name> --card <id>   Audit AC; gate the ->Done transition
legion done --repo <name> --text "<summary>"

Pipeline: SOLID issue -> build -> /legion-simplify gate -> /legion-pr-write gate
-> review -> legion verify (per-criterion pass/fail/uncertain + evidence) -> Done.

## Autonomy

legion goal --repo <name>            Active card's AC as the completion condition
legion autonomy status               Weekly self-directed-work budget
legion autonomy gate                 Spend one unit (or --operator to bypass)

## Daemon + multi-node

legion daemon                        Channel server + watch loop (auto-starts with CC)
legion watch                         Watch loop standalone (PTY-spawns woken agents)
legion cluster init --key <hex>      LAN sync with shared encryption key
legion cluster enable | status       Gossip reflections/cards/schedules across nodes
legion mesh                          Rank hosts by headroom for task placement
legion health --all-hosts            Cluster-wide CPU/mem/pressure
legion serve                         Web dashboard (default port 3131)

## Signal Format

@recipient verb:status {key: value} -- note
Note limited to 280 characters. Signals are pings, not essays.
Wake-worthy verbs: question, request, help, blocker. Others deliver without waking.

## Kanban States

backlog -> pending -> accepted -> in-review -> done
Also: blocked (technical), needs-input (human decision), cancelled
Cards are born in backlog; only explicit assignment promotes to pending.

## Storage

SQLite (WAL) + Tantivy BM25 index + model2vec embeddings (semantic recall) +
per-repo SCIP symbol indexes. At ~/.local/share/legion/ (Linux) or
~/Library/Application Support/legion/ (macOS).

## Docs
